name: Bullock
overview: The bullock in Scripture serves multiple practical and symbolic roles, especially within the Mosaic Law and Israelite worship. It was commonly used for sacrifice, as seen in the daily sin offerings to atone and sanctify the altar (Exodus 29:36), and in the consecration of priests where hands were laid upon the bullock's head (Exodus 29:10). Beyond sacrifice, bullocks were valuable for agricultural work such as plowing and treading grain, with laws ensuring their rest on the Sabbath (Exodus 23:12) and humane treatment during labor. Additionally, the bullock's significance is reflected in Solomon's temple, where twelve bronze bullocks supported the molten sea, symbolizing strength and service.
